newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips drift in wary trade, FOMC looms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips drift in wary trade, FOMC looms.

text.p: U.S. stocks meandered in morning trade on Monday, with traders unwilling to push stocks decisively up or down before tomorrow's Federal Reserve policy-maker meeting, which could change interest rates.

The Dow Jones industrial average was trading off about nine points at 7185 after opening slightly higher in the wake of Friday's late-session slide. The Nasdaq composite was also lower, off over two points at about 1339.
Analysts are split over whether the Federal Open Market Committee will hike short-term rates or let them stand on Tuesday, and if the market is ready for a possible increase.
"The market is doing nothing," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "It is on hold until we see what the Fed does tomorrow."
Traders said market action was quiet and slightly choppy ahead of the meeting. On the New York Stock Exchange, the declining issues outnumbered advancers by about 1037 to 959.
The long bond was also subdued, up 1/32 at a yeild of 6.90 percent compared to Friday's yield of 6.91 percent.
James Crawford, senior vice president at Trevor Stewart Burton & Jacobsen, said: "Odds are we will see more churning with a slightly downward bias for the rest of the week."
